extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment & Discipline, and counsel involved in practitioner discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and regulatory criteria governing exclusion on consent, practitioner misconduct, and obligations of excluded or practicing persons before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. (OED disciplinary rules). Includes specific rule citations and the kinds of conduct that trigger discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation — compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's Affidavit of Resignation must comply with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) for approval of an exclusion on consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the affidavit complies the Director may approve the affidavit and exclude the practitioner on consent; the Final Order notes the OED Director submitted the affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Exclusion on Consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of an affidavit of resignation results in exclusion on consent from practice before the Office in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order requires publication of the order in the OED FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order; excluded practitioners must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and with 11.60 upon any reinstatement request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of an excluded practitioner — 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, including (but not limited to) giving notice of exclusion to clients, filing notices of withdrawal in pending applications, delivering client papers/property, and providing the required 45-day affidavit to OED.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific subsections referenced: 11.58(a) (no practice), 11.58(b)(1)(i) (file notice of withdrawal), 11.58(b)(1)(ii) (notify clients), 11.58(b)(1)(iv) (deliver papers/property and call attention to urgencies), 11.58(b)(2) (45-day affidavit), 11.58(b)(3) (not hold oneself out as authorized), 11.58(c) (not be engaged as practitioner for another), 11.58(e) (not aid others except as salaried employee). The order lists many alleged violations predicated on failure to follow these duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on practicing before the USPTO in violation — 37 C.F.R. § 11.505
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper to practice law before the USPTO in violation of USPTO regulations (e.g., preparing and signing trademark applications, consulting or giving advice about filing documents while excluded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged misconduct includes preparing and signing trademark applications while excluded, consulting or advising customers about trademark or patent filings while excluded, and allowing non-practitioners to prepare/sign/file submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assisting others in unauthorized practice — 37 C.F.R. § 11.505 (assist)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assisting another in practicing before the USPTO in violation of USPTO regulations is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the order: allowing a non-practitioner to prepare, sign, and file trademark documents; allowing non-practitioners to consult with customers in contemplation of filings; failing to supervise contract paralegals who prepared/signed/filed trademark applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not acting with reasonable diligence and promptness — 37 C.F.R. § 11.103
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged failures included not informing clients of abandonment, not taking timely steps to protect client interests, and inadequate supervision or monitoring of assistants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and consultation duties — 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(5), (b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must reasonably consult about means to accomplish client's objectives, keep the client reasonably informed about status, consult about relevant limitations when client expects prohibited assistance, and explain matters sufficiently to permit informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include not informing patent clients their applications had become abandoned, not informing clients of limitations stemming from exclusion, and failing to explain material risks and alternatives for informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty upon termination to protect client's interests — 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon termination of representation, a practitioner must take reasonably practicable steps to protect the client's interests, such as giving reasonable notice and surrendering papers and property to which the client is entitled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged misconduct: not informing patent clients of inability to continue representation after exclusion; not surrendering client files or calling attention to urgent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities regarding non-practitioner assistants — 37 C.F.R. § 11.503
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners are responsible for supervising non-practitioner assistants and ensuring their work complies with rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged failure to supervise/adequately monitor a contract paralegal who impermissibly prepared, signed, and filed trademark applications; allowing non-practitioners to give legal advice or prepare filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities regarding law-related services — 37 C.F.R. § 11.507
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing law-related services, practitioners must ensure such services are distinct from legal services or take reasonable measures so clients understand the nature and that client-practitioner protections may not exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged that The Inventor's Platform provided law-related services not distinct from legal services or failed to make clear the protections of a client-practitioner relationship did not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowingly making false statements of material fact to OED — 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper to knowingly make a false statement of material fact to OED in connection with a disciplinary matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order lists numerous alleged false statements to OED (e.g., misrepresentations about role in The Inventor's Platform, use of aliases, number of trademark filings, compliance with resignation terms, access to IP addresses, whether soliciting customers). OED will treat such falsehoods as disciplinary violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to cooperate with OED investigation — 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to provide non-evasive answers or otherwise failing to cooperate with an OED investigation is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation includes failing to provide non-evasive answers to OED's requests for information and assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candor toward a tribunal — 37 C.F.R. § 11.303
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must be candid toward tribunals; making false or misleading representations to a tribunal or in connection with tribunal matters is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the applicable rule for alleged false/misleading representations to The Florida Bar and other tribunal-adjacent contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowing disobedience of tribunal rules — 37 C.F.R. § 11.304(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowingly disobeying an obligation under the rules of a tribunal (except for open refusal asserting no valid obligation exists) is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failure to comply with prior Final Order (In re Gray) and continuing refusal to follow tribunal-imposed obligations formed the basis for discipline under this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule violations and inducing others to violate rules — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violating or attempting to violate the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, knowingly assisting or inducing another to do so, or doing so through acts of another is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged that respondent violated multiple rules and assisted others (e.g., through The Inventor's Platform) in doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation violates the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many alleged acts fall under this provision: false representations about who drafted applications, misrepresenting fee distributions, using fictitious names, false statements to various authorities and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice is a disciplinary violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include failing to disclose material information to customers and others in ways that interfered with fair administration (e.g., not disclosing relevant case law or prior exclusions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct adversely reflecting on fitness to practice — 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in other conduct that adversely reflects on a practitioner's fitness to practice before the USPTO is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used broadly in the order to encompass conduct such as holding oneself out while excluded, misrepresentations to the public, and other unethical behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invention promotion/invention promoter disclosure requirements (pre-contract disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to entering into a contract for invention promotion services, an invention promoter must disclose in writing certain information to customers, including: (1) total number of inventions evaluated in past five years and how many received positive/negative evaluations; (2) total number of customers who contracted in past five years (with exclusions); (3) total number of customers known to have received a net financial profit as a direct result of services; (4) total number known to have received license agreements as a direct result of services; (5) names and addresses of all previous invention promotion companies with which the promoter or its officers have been affiliated in the prior 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged failure to provide those disclosures in writing to hundreds of The Inventor's Platform customers before contracting, and cited 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(c), 11.804(d), and 11.804(i) as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful representation of practitioner involvement and firm identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must not falsely represent who prepared filings, the practitioner's role (e.g., passive investor vs. active operator), or the names under which a business operates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations include falsely representing that attorneys drafted provisional applications when they were prepared by respondent or contractors, misrepresenting that respondent was a passive investor when he ran day-to-day operations, and not disclosing use of the fictitious name 'Nickolas Farbacks' on filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee disclosure and truthful statements about fee allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Representations to clients about fees and how fees are allocated (e.g., attorney fees collected and paid to practitioners) must be truthful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged The Inventor's Platform represented $485 as attorney fees to be paid to referred practitioners when only $135 was paid and $350 retained, constituting misrepresentation under 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.804(c) and 11.804(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent — adequate information about material risks and alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Clients purportedly waiving conflicts or consenting to courses of conduct must be given adequate information and explanation about material risks and reasonably available alternatives to permit informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged customers signed waivers without being given adequate information or explanations about risks/alternatives, implicating §§ 11.804(c), 11.804(d), and 11.804(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure to referred practitioners about relevant ethics rules/case law
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who refers customers to other practitioners must inform those practitioners of relevant USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct or case law reasonably applicable to the practitioner-customer relationship when the referring practitioner has firsthand knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failure to inform referred practitioners of rules or case law (e.g., In re Schoonover) and failure to disclose exclusion status and true identity while referring customers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding oneself out while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner must not hold himself out as authorized to practice before the USPTO or allow representations (e.g., 'Senior Counsel' internet profile) that imply such authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged misconduct includes being listed as 'Senior Counsel' online while excluded and in inactive status with a state bar, violating §§ 11.58(b)(3) and 11.804 provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthful use of names and aliases on government filings and certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing or causing to be signed fictitious names on government filings with certification under penalty of perjury is improper when the signer knows the name is fictitious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED alleged respondent signed 'Nickolas Farbacks' on Wyoming annual reports and filed them under perjury certification while knowing the alias was fictitious, implicating § 11.804(c) and 11.804(i).
